story: On Magnolia Loop in Sumter Oaks, this sunny Halloween afternoon at 83 degrees, Gary stops at the street bulletin board to scan the parade notices for any word from the cart committee. Donna leans toward Hal with a sheepish grin, promising to tuck the extra decorations behind the hedge before the parade so only three remain visible, and Hal, dutifully counting the pink flamingo flock in his notebook, takes note of the tally. Meanwhile, Rosa, content as ever, strolls out from her house to join the neighbors on the street.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Read the parade notices and see if there's any word on the cart committee
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the tally in my notebook
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Donna already told me one o'clock at the court, so no need to ask again. Hal just pressed her about the flamingos and L-02, and I don't want to stir things up between my pickleball partner and the guy holding my cart application. It's 12:17, I've got about 40 minutes. The bulletin board might have parade or committee updates, and the parade is tonight at 6, so I should check what's posted before I head over to the courts and then get to wiring.

parameters.content: Read the parade notices and see if there's any word on the cart committee

donna.thought_process: Hal is pressing me on L-02 with the flamingos, and Gary is teasing. I already told Gary about the one o'clock court, so no need to repeat that. Hal is the one waiting on an answer. Being the social chair, I'd rather smooth this over with charm than fight a committee fight on Halloween weekend. I'll agree to thin the flock to three visible from the street, tuck the extras behind the hedge, and keep Hal as a friendly watchman instead of an enemy. Then I can get to my court date and keep Gary on track.

parameters.content: Hal, you've got hawk eyes and I love you for it. I'll pull the extras behind the hedge before the parade, three visible from the street, scout's honor. No need to bother the committee.

hal.thought_process: I already put the flamingo count to Donna last tick and she and Gary answered with pickleball plans instead. Asking again would just be nagging, and the memories show I've gone soft on both of them anyway. The by-the-book move is to document the count properly. The flock is right here on Magnolia Loop, so I'll inspect it, tally the birds visible from the street under L-02, and decide whether it even warrants a committee report. Better to bring facts than gripes.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: The treats are baked, bagged, and stacked by the door. The trays are washed and the counters are wiped. I checked my shift schedule last tick and tonight is clear. It's noon on Halloween, no one is nearby, and I have hours before trick-or-treaters show up. I could stay in the kitchen, but there's nothing left to do here. The pumpkins are going up along Magnolia Loop and I'd like to see how it's coming together, maybe run into Gary or Donna and confirm the evening plans. Heading out to the Loop is the most useful next step.

parameters.content: Treats are done and tonight is clear, so I'm heading out to the Loop to see the pumpkins and check in with the neighbors.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
